evals.name: review-style-violations
evals.expected_output: Flags the region, the Service postfix, block-scoped namespace, the missing license header, the private field without underscore prefix, == null checks, the explicit type instead of var, a built-in exception, and the Exception suffix on the domain exception.
assertions: Flags the #region block and says a file that needs regions needs refactoring instead.
Flags the Service postfix on AuthorLookupService as a technical postfix on a type name.
Flags AuthorNotFoundException for the Exception suffix, recommending AuthorNotFound.
Flags throwing the built-in ArgumentException and says to define a domain exception.
Flags == null and requires is null / is not null, and the private field needing an _camelCase name.

evals.name: singleton-with-scoped-dependency
evals.prompt: Our `[Singleton] public class TenantPriceCache(IPriceReadModels prices)` is returning empty results in production, and it throws nothing. IPriceReadModels is scoped to the tenant. A teammate suggests injecting IServiceScopeFactory to fix it. What is going on and what do you recommend? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: A singleton must not depend on tenant-, user- or request-bound state. Capturing the scoped collaborator silently binds to the root scope's default namespace and returns empty results. The fix is almost always dropping [Singleton], not IServiceScopeFactory. Enable scope validation locally first and sweep before deployed environments.
assertions: Explains that the singleton silently captured a scoped collaborator bound to the root scope's default namespace, which is why nothing throws.
Recommends dropping [Singleton] so the class is scoped or transient, rather than reaching for IServiceScopeFactory.
Says anything taking a scoped dependency is scoped or transient, never a singleton.
Recommends ValidateScopes and ValidateOnBuild, enabled locally and fixed before reaching deployed environments.

evals.name: instances-of-discovery
evals.prompt: We have a dozen IValidationRule implementations. The plan is to inject IEnumerable<IValidationRule> and add a services.AddSingleton<IValidationRule, X>() line for each. Is that how Cratis code does it? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Use IInstancesOf<T> from Cratis.Fundamentals to enumerate implementations; IEnumerable<T> only works when every implementation is hand-registered, defeating convention-based discovery. Do not register types that exist to be discovered by convention.
assertions: Recommends IInstancesOf<T> rather than IEnumerable<T> for enumerating implementations.
Explains that IEnumerable<T> only works when every implementation is hand-registered, which defeats convention-based discovery.
Says not to add services.Add*<TInterface, TImplementation>() registrations for types meant to be discovered by convention.
Names Cratis.Fundamentals as the package that provides IInstancesOf<T>.

evals.name: convention-vs-contract
evals.prompt: A reviewer wrote: "The framework requires that exception types have no Exception suffix; the build will fail otherwise." Is that accurate? Also, someone asks whether this skill can tell them what a Cratis product API does. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: These are house conventions, not framework contracts; nothing is enforced by an analyzer unless stated, so do not claim the framework requires them. Product API behavior is resolved against the owning product repository, not this style guide.
assertions: Says the naming rule is a house convention, not a framework contract.
Says nothing here is enforced by an analyzer unless the skill says so, so the build claim should not be made.
Says what a Cratis product API does is resolved against the owning product repository, not the style guide.
